results.title: Kome Shime Traditional Council inducts six new chiefs and queen mothers in Whuti
results.content: The Kome Shime Traditional Council has inducted six new members following a swearing-in ceremony held at Whuti in the Volta Region on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. The ceremony formally welcomed the traditional leaders into the Council, with officials saying the move would strengthen its representation and support traditional governance within the Kome Shime Traditional Area and Anlo State. The newly inducted members are Togbi Agbelom Agbotokor Dzreke II, Divisional Chief of Salo-Sokutsime; Togbi Tsikata Agbodzie II, Divisional Chief of Srogboe; and Mama Amedzor II, Divisional Queenmother of Salo-Sokutsime. The others are Togbi Lagah Doe Dzata V, Sub-Divisional Chief of Whuti; Mama Agume Dzonu II, Sub-Divisional Queenmother of Whuti; and Mama Kordeku II, Sub-Divisional Queenmother of Srogboe.

results.title: Mahama links rising foreign investment to improving economic stability
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama says improving economic stability is strengthening investor confidence in Ghana, with foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows rising to US$2.62 billion in 2025 from US$624 million in 2024.

results.title: Energy Minister pledges inter-ministerial push to unblock Petroleum Hub project
results.content: The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has pledged to lead inter-ministerial engagements to resolve outstanding land acquisition, compensation and financing issues delaying the development of Ghana’s Petroleum Hub.

results.title: Ghana now facilitates 40% of Burkina Faso’s petroleum transit – Jinapor
results.content: Ghana is facilitating the transportation of approximately 40% of Burkina Faso’s petroleum products, up from 15% two years ago, Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has disclosed.

results.title: KGL Foundation screens over 200 people in Techiman for breast cancer and other conditions
results.content: More than 200 residents of Techiman have benefited from a free health screening exercise organised by the KGL Foundation as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The outreach, organised in collaboration with Koranteng Memorial Clinic and AgricoHub, offered screening for breast cancer, blood pressure, Human Papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B and C, and eye conditions, among other services. Organisers said the initiative was intended to promote early detection and preventive healthcare while making screening services more accessible to residents.

results.title: Government develops roadmap to improve maternal healthcare and hospital bed management
results.content: The Deputy Minister for Health, Dr Grace Ayensu-Danquah, says the government is developing a roadmap to address challenges in maternal healthcare and improve the quality of care across all regions.

results.title: GES report identifies teacher divisions, student gangs as factors in Obuasi SHTS unrest
results.content: Ashanti Regional Directorate of the Ghana Education Service (GES) committee that investigated the August 2026 protest at Obuasi Senior High Technical School has found that factions among teachers and student gangs are undermining discipline, staff cohesion and the administration of the school.

results.title: RISE-Ghana urges NDC to reconsider clearance of accused Obuasi SHTS headmaster
results.content: Human rights and sustainable development organisation RISE-Ghana has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to reconsider its decision to clear the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, to contest the party’s constituency chairmanship. The organisation says the decision risks undermining public confidence in state institutions, access to justice and efforts to protect children amid allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at the school. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, and signed by its Executive Director, Awal Ahmed Kariama, RISE-Ghana described the matter as a test of the commitment of political parties and state institutions to child protection and accountability. It argued that the handling of the case could affect the confidence of survivors and their families in the justice system.

results.title: CalBank supports Achimota Golf Club’s Pink Cup in fight against breast cancer
results.content: CalBank PLC has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting initiatives that promote health, strengthen communities and make a meaningful difference in people’s lives, following its sponsorship of the 2026 ONE Pink Cup Golf Tournament organized by the Ladies Section of the Achimota Golf Club. results.title: Breathing Poison: Toxic smoke from Agbogbloshie e-waste burning still making workers sick
results.content: Smoke from burning electronic waste at Agbogbloshie in Accra is filling the air with toxic chemicals, and researchers have long said the harmful effects are already getting into people's bodies — making them sick and, in some cases, killing them. It has been nearly two decades since clear evidence of direct human exposure to e-waste contaminants was found among workers at Agbogbloshie. In a 2012 study, urine samples from 20 male e-waste workers aged between 15 and 42 found significantly higher levels of iron, the flame-retardant antimony, and lead in the urine of the e-waste workers.

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Starting the 2027 Strategic Planning Process
results.content: Strategic planning for 2027 should begin before the current year closes. CEOs who wait until December risk making important decisions under time pressure, relying on incomplete analysis, or carrying existing priorities into the new year without sufficient review. Starting early gives the executive team time to examine current performance, understand market developments, reassess strategic assumptions, and determine what the organization must do differently to achieve its next set of objectives.

results.title: IEAG demands probe into reported MSC office assault, warns of rising tensions at Tema Port
results.content: The Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) has called for an impartial investigation into a reported assault incident at the Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) office at the Tema Port, warning that unresolved operational challenges could trigger further confrontations between port users and service providers.

results.title: IEAG urges Finance Minister to convene emergency meeting over Tema Port crisis
results.content: The Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) has called on the Minister for Finance to convene an emergency stakeholder meeting to address persistent shipping-line delays, terminal disruptions and mounting financial losses at the Tema Port.

results.title: Kwakye Ofosu takes on Bawumia; accuses him of a U-turn on exchange rate stability
results.content: The Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has accused former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia of changing his position on the importance of exchange rate stability in assessing Ghana’s economic performance.

results.title: Is Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15 million suit a face-saving writ?
results.content: If Afenyo-Markin does not go back to court, properly, and make the process public, Ghanaians will believe Sammy Gyamfi. That is not law. That is how public trust works. You cannot file a defective writ, lose on a technicality, and then expect us to clap for you and move on. If Sammy Gyamfi has no evidence, let the court expose him. Let him be made to prove his emphatic claim to strict proof. But if he has the evidence he claims to have, then let it also come out.

results.title: Mahama urges African countries to strengthen mineral deals to retain more resource wealth

results.title: Mahama Ayariga calls for stronger local governance to ensure mining benefits communities
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called for stronger local governance, community participation and accountability in the mining sector to ensure that Africa’s mineral wealth translates into improved living conditions for its people.

results.title: What Is Wrong With Us: When a peaceful election quietly becomes a sad ending for honest businesses
results.content: Ghana’s democratic transitions rightly inspire admiration. It is therefore all the more unfortunate, and deeply worrying, that each change of government can leave committed entrepreneurs unpaid, loyal workers uncertain and promising enterprises struggling to survive.

results.title: NIA opens online Ghana Card replacement service to Ghanaians in 11 countries
results.content: The National Identification Authority (NIA) has introduced an online Ghana Card replacement service for Ghanaians living in 11 countries, allowing them to replace their cards without travelling to Ghana.

results.title: Mahama Ayariga highlights need for African unity in mining to secure local benefits
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has emphasised the need for African countries to adopt coordinated approaches to mineral resource management to ensure that the continent’s natural wealth delivers lasting economic and social benefits.

results.title: Quality and integrity must define Ghanaian brands – Prof. Stephen Adei
results.content: Professor Stephen Adei, Patron of the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), has urged marketing practitioners to help build competitive Ghanaian brands that deliver quality products and services.

results.title: Investors push for Ghana’s return to global capital markets; government says no rush

results.content: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, the Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Administration, has described Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) as central to Ghana’s economic transformation and growth, emphasising the critical role of industry in developing a skilled workforce.

results.title: CHASS demands prompt release of free SHS funds and payment of arrears

results.title: GMA seeks integration of maritime systems to boost trade facilitation

results.title: AU recommends Ghana’s GoldBod model to African countries

results.title: NAGRAT fumes as NDC clears interdicted Obuasi headmaster for election despite sex scandal

results.title: Christian Council condemns insults in Ghanaian politics
